def: 1. (the atmosphere) the mixture of gases that surrounds the earth · 2. a mixture of gases that surrounds another planet or a star · 3. the air in a room or in a small space · 4. the feeling or mood that you have in a particular place or situation.
All the water on the earth's surface, including oceans, seas, rivers, lakes and the water vapour in the air; the water component of the earth.
The rigid outer part of the earth, including the crust and the upper part of the mantle; broken into the tectonic plates that carry the continents.
A colourless, odourless chemical element (symbol O) that exists as a gas in the atmosphere and is essential for respiration in most living things.
A compound formed when oxygen combines with another chemical element.
A colourless, odourless gas (chemical formula CO₂) produced by burning carbon-containing material, by breathing, and by natural processes; the main greenhouse gas from human activity.
A colourless, odourless, very light gas (symbol H) that combines with oxygen to form water; the most common element in the universe.
1. the hard central part of a fruit, especially an apple. 2. the central part of the earth, or of any object. 3. the most important or basic part of something.
1. the hard outer layer or surface of bread, a pie, etc. 2. a layer of something hard, especially one that forms on top of a softer or liquid thing. 3. (geology) the outer layer of the earth.

1. (geology) the part of the earth between the crust and the core. 2. a loose, sleeveless cloak worn over other clothes. 3. a covering layer of something. 4. (figurative) a role or responsibility taken on by someone.
The distance of a place east or west of a line that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole through Greenwich, London, measured in degrees.
1. the distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees. 2. (figurative) freedom to choose what to do or say.
1. the height above sea level. 2. (usually plural) a place that is high above sea level.
1. the line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet. 2. (usually plural, figurative) the limit of a person's knowledge, experience or interest.
1. an unexpected event, such as a flood, storm or accident, that causes great damage or loss of life. 2. (informal) a complete failure; a very bad person or thing.
A small accident or piece of bad luck that is not very serious.
1. (of a natural event) causing many people to suffer. 2. causing a lot of problems for people.
An event that causes great damage, suffering or loss; a disaster, especially one that affects many people.
To put somebody or something in a situation in which they could be harmed, lost or destroyed.
To put something important such as a plan, a job or a relationship at risk of being harmed or lost.
Causing damage or harm; wanting or tending to destroy things.
A climate pattern in which the surface water of the eastern Pacific Ocean becomes unusually warm, affecting weather in many parts of the world; the opposite phase is called La Niña.
1. (noun) a building made mainly of glass, used for growing plants that need warmth and protection. 2. (as modifier) of or producing the greenhouse effect: greenhouse gas, greenhouse warming.

1. a fact or an event in nature or society, especially one that is not fully understood. 2. a person or thing that is very successful or impressive. · Plural (sense 1): phenomena /fəˈnɒmɪnə/; (sense 2, NAmE): phenomenons.
A small, smooth, round stone, especially one found on a beach or in a river.
1. a piece of iron or other material that can attract iron or steel. 2. (figurative) a person, place or thing that attracts many people.
Rock or earth from which metal or valuable minerals can be obtained.

1. (noun) a solid, naturally occurring substance that is not a plant or animal, such as gold, salt or quartz. 2. (BrE, plural, often minerals) = mineral water: “a glass of minerals” (BrE). 3. (adjective) of or relating to minerals: mineral deposits / mineral water.

1. a hard, usually white or patterned stone, used for buildings and statues. 2. (usually plural) a small glass ball used in children's games. 3. (adjective) made of marble; figurative: cold or smooth like marble.
A hard mineral, often in the form of clear or coloured crystals, used in making watches, clocks and electronic circuits.
A very hard, usually grey rock, used for buildings and monuments.
1. (noun) a light, gentle wind. 2. (informal, countable) something that is easy to do. 3. (verb) to move quickly and lightly.
1. (noun) a sudden, short burst of wind, rain, sound, or an emotion. 2. (verb) (of wind) to blow in gusts.
1. a very strong wind; on the Beaufort scale, a gale is roughly force 8–10. 2. (figurative) a sudden loud burst of noise, e.g. laughter.
A violent storm with extremely strong winds and heavy rain, especially in the western Atlantic Ocean. (Same phenomenon is called a typhoon in the western Pacific and a cyclone in the Indian Ocean.)

A violent storm with very strong winds that spin extremely fast and form a funnel-shaped cloud that touches the ground; common in central US in spring and summer. (Also called twister in informal NAmE.)
A violent tropical storm with very strong winds, occurring especially in the western Pacific Ocean. (Same phenomenon as a hurricane in the Atlantic / a cyclone in the Indian Ocean.)

1. a period of heavy rain in summer in South Asia; the rain that falls during this period. 2. a wind in South Asia that blows from the south-west in summer, bringing rain, and the north-east in winter.
A mountain or hill with a hole at the top through which gases, hot liquid rock (lava) and ash can escape from deep inside the earth.
1. (of a volcano) to throw out burning rocks, ash and lava. 2. (of a person or feelings) to become suddenly and violently loud or active. 3. (of violence, fighting, etc.) to start suddenly.
Hot, liquid rock found below the earth's surface. When it reaches the surface it is called lava.
Relating to the branch of physics that deals with the relationship between heat, work, temperature and energy.
A form of air pollution that is a mixture of smoke and fog, especially in big cities.
1. (noun, usually plural) smoke or gas that has an unpleasant smell, especially from a chemical or car engine. 2. (verb) to be very angry; to give off fumes.
1. (noun) a thin cloud of very small drops of water in the air, near the ground. 2. a film of moisture that makes it difficult to see clearly. 3. (verb) to cover or become covered with mist.
An extremely large wave in the sea caused, for example, by an earthquake under the sea.
A situation in which an area of land is covered with water, especially when this causes damage; the action of being covered with water.
1. a large amount of water moving very quickly and strongly. 2. a sudden large amount of something that comes in a stream.
A long period of time when there is little or no rain, causing serious problems such as water shortage.
A sudden, violent shaking of the ground, caused by movement of the earth's crust or by volcanic activity.
1. relating to or caused by earthquakes. 2. (figurative) very great or important; causing a major change.
1. a mass of snow, ice and rock that suddenly slides down a mountain. 2. (figurative) a very large amount of something that arrives suddenly.
1. the physical features of a piece of land, e.g. its hills, valleys, rivers or forests. 2. (figurative) a field of activity, knowledge or experience.

1. (noun) everything you can see when you look across a large area of land, especially in the country. 2. (noun, figurative) the way a subject or situation is shaped at a particular time. 3. (verb) to make a park or garden more attractive by adding plants, paths, etc.

1. one of the seven large land masses of the earth (Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia/Oceania, Antarctica). 2. (BrE, informal, humorous) a long time without using the toilet.
1. (noun) a large natural hole in the side of a cliff or hill, or under the ground. 2. (verb, cave in) to fall down or collapse inward.
A steep, high face of rock, especially one by the sea.
A large mass of ice that forms on mountains from compacted snow and moves very slowly down a valley.
1. (noun) an area of ground that is very wet or covered with water and is difficult to walk through. 2. (verb) to make somebody feel so overwhelmed that they cannot deal with things.

1. an area of low, flat land shaped like a triangle, where a river splits into smaller channels before entering the sea. 2. (mathematics / science) a change or difference in a quantity. 3. the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet (Δ, δ).
A large area of flat dry land.
An area of fairly flat high ground.
An area in a desert where there is water and plants.
A model of the earth, or the earth itself.
Half of the earth, especially the northern or southern half divided by the equator, or the eastern or western half divided by a meridian.
An imaginary line around the earth at an equal distance from the North and South Poles.
Connected with the North Pole or the region around it; extremely cold.
Connected with the South Pole or the region around it.
1. either of the two points at the exact top and bottom of the earth. 2. either of the two ends of a magnet. 3. either of two opposite opinions, ideas, or situations.
1. connected with the North or South Pole. 2. (figurative) completely opposite.
1. an imaginary line through the middle of an object, around which the object turns. 2. a fixed line used for measurement on a graph.
To become worse.
1. to make an illness, a problem or a situation worse. 2. (informal) to annoy somebody.
1. to make a situation or the condition of something worse. 2. to make somebody feel they have less value.
1. to make a piece of equipment, computer, or service better. 2. to give somebody a better seat, room, etc. Noun: an improvement.
1. (of wind, water, etc.) to wear away soil, rock, etc. 2. to gradually destroy or reduce something.
Connected with the Mediterranean Sea or the countries around it.
Connected with the Atlantic Ocean.
Connected with the Pacific Ocean.
1. one of the five very large areas of salt water on the earth. 2. (informal) a very large amount of something.
Connected with the sea; found in the sea.
1. the act of finding your way from one place to another, especially at sea or in the air. 2. the act of moving a boat, ship, or aircraft.
1. a part of the sea that is partly surrounded by land, larger than a bay. 2. (figurative) a wide gap or difference.
An area of sand or small stones beside the sea or a lake.
The land beside or near the sea.
The land along the edge of the sea, a lake, or a wide river.
1. the regular rise and fall of the sea. 2. a tendency or movement in a particular direction.
Happening or being used now. Noun: 1. a flow of water, air, or electricity in a particular direction. 2. a feeling or tendency.
A small stream.
1. a small narrow river. 2. a continuous flow of liquid, gas, or data. Verb: to flow continuously.
1. a place, person, or thing that something comes from. 2. the start of a river.
1. not deep. 2. (figurative) not showing serious thought.
1. on or near the surface only. 2. not studying or looking at something in depth.
1. smooth and level; without curves or slopes. 2. dull, lacking interest. Noun: an apartment.
1. having a flat surface with no lumps or rough areas. 2. happening without problems.
1. not smooth or flat. 2. not exact. 3. difficult or unpleasant.
Covered with or containing sand.
1. covered with stones. 2. showing no friendliness or warmth.
Going straight up or down from a surface; at a right angle to the ground.
1. rising or falling sharply. 2. (informal) higher than reasonable, especially of a price.
1. (of lines or surfaces) at the same distance from each other at every point. 2. (figurative) similar in some way and happening at the same time.
1. small in width. 2. (figurative) limited in scope. Verb: to become narrower.
The group of islands in the Pacific Ocean, including Australia, New Zealand, Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia.
The main area of land of a country, not including islands.
An area of land that is almost surrounded by water but joined to a larger piece of land.
1. the regular pattern of weather conditions of a particular place. 2. (figurative) the general attitude or situation at a particular time.
1. the conditions of rain, sun, wind, etc. at a particular time. Verb: to come through something safely.
The scientific study of the atmosphere and weather.
1. not very strong, cold, or severe. 2. (of a person) gentle and kind.
1. the system that keeps a building warm. 2. the process of becoming warm.
1. average in amount, size, etc. 2. keeping within reasonable limits. Verb: to make or become less extreme.
1. at a fairly high temperature. 2. showing kindness or enthusiasm. Verb: to make or become warm.
1. connected with heat. 2. (of clothing) designed to keep you warm.
The hottest part of the earth, between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
1. (of land or climate) very dry, with little rain. 2. (figurative) dull and uninteresting.
Slightly wet, especially in a pleasant way.
Slightly wet, often in an unpleasant way. Noun: moisture on surfaces or in the air.
Warm and damp.
1. covered with snow. 2. (of weather) when snow is falling.
1. a white powder that forms on surfaces when the temperature is below freezing. 2. a period of weather cold enough to freeze water. Verb: to cover with frost.
1. small balls of ice that fall from the sky. 2. a lot of something arriving at the same time. Verb: 1. to fall as hail. 2. to call out to attract attention.
1. (of ice or snow) to turn to water. 2. (figurative) to become friendlier. Noun: a period of warmer weather that melts snow and ice.
1. to make somebody cold. 2. (figurative) to frighten. Noun: a feeling of coldness or fear.
1. (of water) to turn to ice. 2. to keep food at a very cold temperature. 3. to stop moving. Noun: a period of very cold weather.
1. (formal) very cold. 2. (figurative) unfriendly.
To shake, especially because you are cold, afraid or excited.
To shake slightly, especially because you are cold or frightened.
1. the loud noise that you hear during a storm. 2. a deep loud sound. Verb: to make a loud noise.
1. a flash of bright light in the sky during a storm. 2. (adjective) very fast or sudden.
1. with strong wind, heavy rain, and possibly lightning. 2. (figurative) full of anger or strong emotion.
A lot of rain in a short time.
The total amount of rain that falls in a particular area during a particular period.
1. to shake small drops or pieces of something over a surface. 2. (of rain) to fall lightly. Noun: a light rain or a small amount.
An arch of different colours that appears in the sky when the sun shines through rain.
1. a short period of rain. 2. an act of washing your body standing under a stream of water. Verb: to wash or to rain briefly.
Connected with a scale of temperature in which water freezes at 0° and boils at 100°.
How hot or cold something is, measured with a thermometer.
A statement about what is going to happen in the future, especially about the weather. Verb: to predict.
1. the pointed top of a mountain. 2. the highest level or value. Verb: to reach the highest point.
1. to climb up something. 2. to fix something in position. Noun: a mountain (used in names, e.g. Mount Everest).
A very high hill, usually with steep sides.
1. a line of mountains. 2. the limits of something. Verb: to vary between limits.
A long narrow hill or mountain top.
1. a surface that is higher at one end than the other. 2. (skiing) a mountain used for skiing. Verb: to slant.
An area of low land between hills or mountains, often with a river flowing through it.
The sloping side of a hill.
1. to fail to notice or consider something. 2. to have a view of something from above. Noun: (US) a view from above.
Connected with or in the south of a place.
The direction that is between south and east.
The direction that is between south and west.
The direction that is between north and east.
The direction that is between north and west.
Connected with or in the east of a place.
Connected with or from the East, especially East Asia (an old-fashioned or formal word).
Certain to happen; unavoidable.
Impossible to change back to a previous condition.
In a way that is not regular or even.
Not suitable or appropriate in a particular situation.
Different from what is usual or expected, especially in a way that is worrying or dangerous.
1. solid material that settles at the bottom of a liquid. 2. matter carried by water and deposited on the river bed or the sea floor.
1. sand, mud, etc. carried by flowing water and left on the land. 2. fine sand. Verb: to fill or block with silt.
1. full of or covered with mud. 2. (of a colour) dull brown.
A type of heavy sticky earth used to make pots and bricks.
1. any substance that makes something dirty, especially when it is on the surface of something. 2. loose earth or soil.
Connected with the countryside, not the city.
An area of a town or city that is away from the centre, where mostly houses are.
The parts of a town or city that are farthest from the centre.
1. far away from other places or towns. 2. (of a chance) very small. 3. not friendly.
1. (of a place) empty and without people, making you feel sad. 2. (of a person) very unhappy.
1. far away in space or time. 2. not friendly; cold.
Next to or very near something, especially with nothing in between.
1. poisonous. 2. (figurative) very unpleasant or harmful.
1. the process of polluting something. 2. substances that pollute something.
A substance that pollutes something, especially air or water.
To make a substance, area, etc. dirty or harmful by adding a substance that is dangerous.
1. the study of the earth, including rocks, soil, etc. 2. the rocks and soil of a particular area.
1. the line that divides two countries or areas. 2. a strip around the edge of something. Verb: 1. to share a border with. 2. to be next to.
1. the empty space at the side of a page. 2. the amount of something that is left over. 3. the edge of an area.
1. a strip of hair or fabric that hangs down. 2. the outer edge of an area. Adjective: not part of the main group.
1. a flat round dish for food. 2. (geology) one of the very large pieces of rock that form the earth's surface.
Broken pieces of something that has been destroyed.
1. a thin line on a surface where it has broken but not split into pieces. 2. a sharp sound. Verb: 1. to break without separating into pieces. 2. to make a sharp sound.
1. an empty space between two things. 2. a difference between two groups or things. 3. a missing part.
Very good; excellent.
1. impressive because of size, importance or style. 2. (informal) very good or enjoyable.
Extremely attractive and impressive; deserving praise.
(informal) excellent; very good.
Attracting your attention because it is exciting or unusual.
1. connected with drama or the theatre. 2. exciting and impressive. 3. sudden and noticeable.
1. a large area of land that has never been developed or used for farming. 2. a place that is wild and empty.
A large area of land, usually in a hot region, where there is very little rain and few plants. Verb: /dɪˈzɜːt/ to leave somebody without help.
To cut down the trees in a large area.
1. (of land) not good enough to grow plants on. 2. (of a tree or plant) producing no fruit. 3. (figurative) producing no useful result.
1. (of land or soil) able to produce good crops. 2. (of a person, animal or plant) able to produce young, fruit or seeds. 3. (of a mind) producing a lot of ideas.
To put fertiliser on soil to make plants grow better.
Connected with the sun.
Connected with the moon.
1. a page or set of pages showing the days, weeks and months of a particular year. 2. a system for measuring time.
The time in the morning when the sun appears.
The time in the evening when the sun disappears.

1. an occasion when the moon passes between the earth and the sun so that you cannot see all or part of the sun. 2. a similar occasion when the earth passes between the sun and the moon. Verb: 1. to cause an eclipse. 2. (figurative) to make somebody seem less important.
The time of day when the light is almost gone but it is not yet dark.
1. (in some religions) the place where God or the gods live and where good people go after they die. 2. (informal) a place or situation that makes you very happy.
1. (in some religions) a beautiful place where good people go after they die. 2. a place that is extremely beautiful or pleasant.
1. the light of the sun. 2. (informal) a word used to address somebody in a friendly way.
1. an area that is dark and cool because the sun does not reach it. 2. a degree of a colour. Verb: to protect from direct light.
1. a dark shape on a surface that is made when something stands between a light and the surface. 2. a small amount of something. Verb: to follow somebody closely.
A mass of very small drops of liquid in the air, like steam.
1. (of a liquid) to turn into a gas. 2. to disappear.
1. to move around freely within a system. 2. to pass from one person to another. 3. to send something to each person in a group.

1. (formal) to make something happen suddenly or sooner. 2. (chemistry) to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution. 3. (of rain, snow, etc.) to fall. Noun: /prɪˈsɪpɪtət/ a substance separated from a solution.
1. a natural or artificial lake where water is stored. 2. a large amount of something that is available but not yet used.
A place where water falls from a high rock or cliff.
1. a structure from which water is sent up into the air by a pump. 2. a source of something.
1. the season between winter and summer. 2. a place where water comes naturally out of the ground. Verb: to jump up suddenly.
Very small drops of water that form on cold surfaces during the night.
1. to make a liquid or other substance flow from a container. 2. (of rain) to fall heavily.
1. (of a liquid) to flow away. 2. to make a liquid flow away from something. 3. (figurative) to use up somebody's energy, money, etc. Noun: a pipe that takes away water or liquid waste.
1. (of a liquid) to fall in small drops. 2. to make liquid fall in small drops. Noun: a small drop of liquid.
1. to die because you cannot breathe under water. 2. (figurative) to cover or be covered by a liquid completely.
1. (of wind) to move or be moving. 2. to move air from your mouth. 3. to make a sound by pushing air through an instrument. Noun: 1. a hit. 2. a sudden event.
1. to breathe quickly and with difficulty. 2. to blow smoke or steam. Noun: 1. a small amount of smoke, air, etc. 2. a light pastry.
1. (of a liquid) to flow out suddenly and in large amounts. 2. (figurative) to talk or express admiration in an excessive way. Noun: a sudden flow of liquid.
1. (of a substance) thick; difficult to see through. 2. (of people or things) packed closely together. 3. (informal) stupid.
1. the quality of being very strong, concentrated or extreme. 2. the strength of a colour, light, sound, etc.
Involving a lot of work or activity in a short time; concentrated.
1. to come out of somewhere. 2. to become known.
1. a sudden bright light. 2. a short piece of information on a screen. Verb: 1. to shine brightly for a moment. 2. to pass quickly.
1. to stay on the surface of a liquid. 2. to move slowly in the air or on water. Noun: a small floating object.
1. the conditions that surround somebody or something. 2. the natural world, especially as affected by human activity.
That is around or near something.
1. the state that somebody or something is in. 2. something that must happen before something else can happen. Verb: 1. to train. 2. (formal) to influence the way somebody thinks or behaves.
All the circumstances and things that are happening at a particular time and in a particular place.
1. the whole universe, especially the physical world; all the things in the world that are not made by people. 2. the basic quality or character of something.
1. existing in nature; not made or caused by humans. 2. as you would expect; normal.
1. made or produced by humans rather than occurring naturally. 2. not sincere; not genuine.
Made by combining chemical substances rather than being natural; artificial.
1. (BrE) a liquid obtained from petroleum, used as fuel for motor vehicles. 2. (US: gasoline) the same substance.
1. any substance like air that is neither a solid nor a liquid. 2. (US) = petrol. 3. a gas used for heating or cooking.
A liquid obtained from petroleum, used as fuel for motor vehicles (NAmE; BrE: petrol).
A dark thick oil obtained from under the ground, used for making petrol and many other substances.
